irs_sch_a_2025_instructions.title: Instructions for Schedule A (Form 1040) (2025)

schedule_1a_2025.title: Schedule 1-A (Form 1040) 2025 — Additional Deductions
schedule_1a_2025.note: Part II tips: max 25,000, MAGI 150,000/300,000, $100 per $1,000 rounded DOWN. Part III overtime: 12,500/25,000, MAGI 150,000/300,000, $100 per $1,000 rounded DOWN. schedule_8812_2025.title: Schedule 8812 (Form 1040) 2025

form_1040es.note: 110% safe harbor applies when prior-year AGI exceeded $150,000 ($75,000 if MFS).

statutory_non_indexed_credits.title: IRS - American Opportunity Tax Credit; IRC 21 and 25A
statutory_non_indexed_credits.note: AOTC ($2,500 max, 40% refundable, $80k-$90k / $160k-$180k phase-out) and the Child and Dependent Care Credit ($3,000/$6,000 expense limits, 35% to 20% between $15,000 and $43,000 AGI) are fixed by statute and are NOT inflation-indexed, so one shared block serves every year.

ftc_904j.title: IRS Instructions for Form 1116 — IRC 904(j) election to claim the FTC without Form 1116
ftc_904j.note: IRC 904(j) election: a taxpayer may claim the foreign tax credit directly on Schedule 3 (Form 1040), Part I, line 1 without filing Form 1116 when (1) ALL foreign-source gross income is passive-category income, (2) it was reported on a qualified payee statement (1099-DIV Box 7, 1099-INT Box 6, K-1/K-3, etc.), and (3) total creditable foreign taxes are $300 or less ($600 if MFJ). Not available to estates/trusts. The election permanently forfeits FTC carryback/carryforward for that year. $300/$600 limits are statutory and not inflation-indexed, so one shared block serves every year.

ira2022_energy_credits.title: IRA-2022 clean-energy credits — IRC 30D / 25E / 25C / 25D (per-credit IRS sources below)
ira2022_energy_credits.note: All figures statutory/non-indexed (identical 2023-2025). §30D new clean vehicle: max $7,500; MAGI caps MFJ/QSS $300k, HoH $225k, single/MFS $150k (lesser of current or prior year, IRC 30D(f)(10)(B)); MSRP $80k (SUV/truck/van) / $55k (other) — IRS Topic B https://www.irs.gov/newsroom/topic-b-frequently-asked-questions-about-income-and-price-limitations-for-the-new-clean-vehicle-credit . §25E previously-owned clean vehicle: lesser of $4,000 or 30% of sale price, sale price <= $25,000; MAGI MFJ/QSS $150k, HoH $112,500, single/MFS $75k (lesser of current/prior year, IRC 25E(b)(2)(B)) — IRS https://www.irs.gov/credits-deductions/used-clean-vehicle-credit . §25C energy-efficient home improvement: 30% of cost; $1,200 general annual limit + separate $2,000 limit for heat pumps/heat-pump water heaters/biomass stoves; sub-caps windows/skylights $600, exterior doors $250/door ($500 total), home energy audit $150 — IRS https://www.irs.gov/credits-deductions/energy-efficient-home-improvement-credit and FS-2025-01 https://www.irs.gov/pub/taxpros/fs-2025-01.pdf . §25D residential clean energy: 30% of qualified expenditure, no annual dollar cap (fuel cells $500/half-kW only); nonrefundable, unused carries forward (IRC 25D(c)) — IRS FS-2025-01 https://www.irs.gov/pub/taxpros/fs-2025-01.pdf .

obbba_energy_terminations.title: IRS FAQs — modification of §§25C/25D/25E/30D/45W under Public Law 119-21 (OBBBA)
obbba_energy_terminations.note: OBBBA (Pub. L. 119-21) terminated the clean-energy credits on an accelerated schedule: §§30D/25E/45W — no credit for vehicles acquired after 2025-09-30 ('acquired' = written binding contract + payment, incl. a nominal down payment or trade-in, on or before that date); §25C — property placed in service after 2025-12-31; §25D — expenditures made after 2025-12-31. 2023 and 2024 blocks carry NO terminated_after key (credits ran all year pre-OBBBA); 2026 has no energy_credits block at all. Same source cited by the termination table in references/credits_guide.md.

edd_de44_2025.title: 2025 California Employer's Guide (DE 44), EDD

ftb_2025_540es.title: 2025 Instructions for Form 540-ES

CA AGI at or above $1,000,000 ($500,000 MFS) must use 90% of the CURRENT year — the prior-year safe harbor is unavailable.

irc_168k_bonus.title: 26 USC 168(k) (bonus depreciation), as amended by Pub. L. 119-21 (OBBBA)
irc_168k_bonus.note: Pre-OBBBA TCJA phasedown (former 168(k)(6)(A)): 80% (2023), 60% (2024), 40% (2025). OBBBA (Pub. L. 119-21, enacted 2025-07-04) restored 100% as the default in 168(k)(1)(A) for property acquired after Jan 19, 2025 and placed in service after that date; property acquired on/before Jan 19, 2025 keeps the pre-OBBBA schedule (40% for 2025). A 168(k)(10) transition election allows 40% (or 60% for long-production/aircraft) in lieu of 100% for the first year ending after Jan 19, 2025. 2026 default 100%.

obbba_statute_2026.title: OBBBA personal deductions (Pub. L. 119-21) — IRC 151(d)(5)(C), 224, 225, 163(h)(4)
obbba_statute_2026.note: 2026 amounts are identical to 2025: none of the four OBBBA personal deductions (senior bonus IRC 151(d)(5)(C); tips IRC 224; overtime IRC 225; car-loan interest IRC 163(h)(4)) are indexed for inflation. Senior bonus $6,000 (6% phase-out over $75,000 single / $150,000 MFJ); tips $25,000 ($150,000/$300,000, $100 per $1,000 rounded down); overtime $12,500/$25,000 (same phase-out); car-loan interest $10,000 ($100,000/$200,000, $200 per $1,000 rounded up). Effective 2025-2028. Confirmed non-indexed in statute text. OBBBA §70105 also widened the §199A(b)(3)(B) phase-in range to $75,000 (single/HoH/MFS) / $150,000 (MFJ) for TY after 12/31/2025 and added §199A(i): a $400 minimum deduction for an 'applicable taxpayer' with ≥$1,000 aggregate QBI from active (material-participation) trades/businesses; the $400 is the GREATER of the normal deduction or $400 and overrides the §199A(a)(2) overall taxable-income limit.

irc_408d8_qcd.title: IRC 408(d)(8) — Qualified Charitable Distribution limit (pre-2024 statutory)
irc_408d8_qcd.note: $100,000 aggregate annual QCD limit, fixed by statute 2016-2023. SECURE 2.0 Act section 112 (Pub. L. 117-328, Div. T) added inflation indexing beginning 2024 (Notice 2023-75 raised it to $105,000).

usc_199a_qbi_statute.title: 26 USC 199A — Qualified business income (as amended by Pub. L. 119-21 §§70105, 70201(d))
usc_199a_qbi_statute.note: §199A(a): deduction = lesser of combined QBI amount or 20% of (taxable income − net capital gain); amended 'except as provided in subsection (i)'. §199A(b)(1)(A)/(c): 20% QBI rate and 20% REIT/PTP rate. §199A(b)(2)(B): W-2 wage/UBIA limit = greater of 50% of W-2 wages or 25% of W-2 wages + 2.5% of UBIA. §199A(e)(3): net capital gain per §1(h)(11) includes qualified dividends. §199A(i)(1): for an 'applicable taxpayer' (aggregate QBI from active—materially-participated—trades/businesses ≥ $1,000 per §199A(i)(2)), deduction = GREATER of the normally-computed deduction or $400; this OVERRIDES the §199A(a)(2) overall taxable-income limit. $400/$1,000 fixed for 2026, inflation-adjusted (nearest $5) for TY after 2026.

irs_form_8995a_instructions.title: Instructions for Form 8995-A (2025) — QBI Deduction
irs_form_8995a_instructions.note: Part II lines 4-11: line 5 = 50% of W-2 wages; line 6 = 25% of W-2 wages; line 8 = 2.5% of UBIA; line 10 = greater of line 5 or (line 6 + line 8); line 11 = lesser of 20% of QBI or line 10. SSTB list (Reg §1.199A-5): health, law, accounting, consulting, financial services, performing arts, athletics, and the 'principal asset is the reputation or skill' catch-all. The tool ASKS the user for SSTB status rather than inferring it.

state_top_marginal_rates._note: TOP MARGINAL rates for rough estimation only — NOT flat effective rates. Treating CA's top marginal rate as flat overstated CA tax by ~132% at $200K MFJ (finding C1). Use the 'states' block for any state with real brackets.
